source.name: Mistral AI, life-cycle analysis of Mistral Large 2 (2025)
source.quote: the marginal impacts of inference, more precisely the use of our AI assistant Le Chat for a 400-token response - excluding users’ terminals: 1.14 gCO₂e, 45 mL of water, and 0.16 mg of Sb eq.

formula: A session is one Claude Code transcript: the file <session id>.jsonl in the session's project folder under the Claude config folder's projects folder (~/.claude/projects unless CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR moves it). Only that file is read. The files under <session id>/subagents/ are not read, so a subagent's tokens do not count.
The file is read as UTF-8 and split on the line feed. Each line is one JSON value. A line that does not parse, the unfinished last line of a file still being written included, is skipped.
A line counts when it is an object whose type is "assistant", whose isSidechain is not true, whose message.id is a non-empty string and whose message.usage is an object. Every other line is skipped.

The four token kinds are input, output, cacheRead and cacheWrite, read from message.usage under the names in usageFields. A field that is missing, or is not a finite number of zero or more, reads as 0.

Claude Code writes one line per content block of a reply, so one assistant message is on several lines that share a message.id. Lines are grouped by message.id and the message counts once: for each kind, the largest value among its lines.
A session's tokens of a kind are the sum of that kind over its messages. Everything the transcript holds counts, the messages a resumed or forked session carried over included.

ml = (input * mlPerThousandTokens.input + output * mlPerThousandTokens.output + cacheRead * mlPerThousandTokens.cacheRead + cacheWrite * mlPerThousandTokens.cacheWrite) / 1000, in IEEE 754 double precision, the four products added left to right in that order and the sum divided once.
Rounding is half up everywhere: round(x) = floor(x + 0.5).

The volume is shown in one of two units. If round(ml) is less than display.litresFromMl, the text is round(ml) in decimal digits, a space, display.millilitreUnit. Otherwise it is fixed(ml, display.litresFromMl, display.litreDecimals), a space, display.litreUnit.

fixed(x, per, d): n = round(x * 10^d / per), multiplied before it is divided. The text is the whole part of n / 10^d in decimal digits, then display.decimalSeparator, then the remainder of n / 10^d padded with leading zeros to d digits. No digit grouping, no exponent, and nothing is taken from the locale.
Glasses are fixed(ml, glassMl, display.glassDecimals). The host words the unit.
The figure is an estimate and is labelled as one wherever it is shown, with source.name readable beside it or one step away.
derivation: The source gives one figure per reply: the volume in source.quote for a 400-token Le Chat response. Divided by 400 and multiplied by 1000 it is mlPerThousandTokens.output.

It is the only first-party figure that states a token count next to the water volume, so it needs one division and no guess at a reply's length. The page was published on 22 July 2025; the study was done with Carbone 4 and ADEME and peer-reviewed by Resilio and Hubblo.

Input, cache read and cache write are 0. The source says nothing about prompt length or input tokens, and whatever prompt processing a typical exchange involved is already inside its one figure, so charging input separately would count it twice.
The figure is a life-cycle one (Water Consumption Potential): data-centre cooling, the electricity behind it and the manufacture of the servers. It leaves out the user's device and training.

It sits at the top of the published range. Google's median Gemini prompt (0.26 mL, arXiv 2508.15734) and Sam Altman's average ChatGPT query (0.000085 gallons) are over a hundred times lower per reply, count cooling water only or give no scope, and state no token count.
assumptions: Water scales linearly with output tokens.
A Mistral token and a Claude token are the same size.

Claude costs what Mistral Large 2 on Le Chat cost in 2024-25. It is a different model on other hardware in other data centres; this is the largest unknown and the reason the figure is called an estimate.
Thinking tokens count, since Claude Code reports them inside output_tokens.
